scope: Healthcare marketing and health economics for Applied Health Sciences students (laboratory, imaging and other programmes): whether marketing concepts are correct and correctly applied to health services, whether promotion is taught within professional ethics and Egyptian regulation, and whether every health-economic calculation is right.
criteria: Each marketing concept (marketing mix, segmentation, life cycle, pricing methods, channels, push and pull) is defined correctly and matches standard marketing texts.
Every concept is applied to health services, not only to medicines, with realistic examples from laboratories, imaging centres, hospitals or devices.
Patients are not treated as ordinary consumers where they are not: who decides, who pays and who is harmed are stated correctly for each example.
Promotion, advertising and sales techniques are taught within professional ethics; nothing endorses misleading, inducement-based or unlawful promotion of health services or medicines.
Statements about Egyptian regulation, pricing control and health insurance are current and attributed to the responsible authority.
Cost categories (direct medical, direct non-medical, indirect, intangible, opportunity, incremental) are classified correctly in every example.
Economic-evaluation methods are chosen correctly for the outcome type (CMA only with demonstrated equivalence; CEA natural units; CUA QALYs; CBA money).
Every ratio (CER, ICER, benefit-cost, cost per QALY) is computed correctly, carries its unit, and is read with the right decision rule, including dominance.
Perspective (patient, provider, payer, society) is stated for each analysis and the costs counted match it.
Perspective boxes for the laboratory and imaging programmes are accurate for those professions and balanced between them.
exclusions: Do not request advanced econometrics or modelling beyond an introductory course.
Do not request marketing plans for named commercial products.
evidence_expectations: Quote the exact text and give file and line for every finding.
Recompute any number challenged, and show the recomputation.
Give replacement text, not only a critique.
Cite a standard marketing or health-economics text, or the regulator's document, for any corrected definition or rule.
